contradictions.fact: Summit-day line: direct south/southeast-flank scramble vs. Cloudy Pass + East Ridge

claims.says: the standard route climbs the peak's south side above Lyman Lake
hike cross-country across open meadow, then up talus and scree (Class 2) on the south side of the mountain
roughly 16 miles up the Railroad Creek Trail to Lyman Lake (no ridge, pass, or Magnolia Mine mentioned)
South/east flank talus-scree slope ... trending onto its south and east side; there is no tread and no cairns
Cross the meadow, round onto the south and southeast side, and climb to it [the snowfield]... a notch on the crest from which the ridge runs to the top
East Ridge summit push ... Hike up to Cloudy Pass, then leave trail to gain the class 2+ East Ridge, skirting old mine workings near Magnolia Mine before following the ridge crest to the summit
East Ridge summit push ... Hike up to Cloudy Pass, then leave trail to gain the class 2…

contradictions.why: overview, beta, approach, waypoints and approach_variants (5 independent fields) unanimously describe a direct cross-country scramble up the south/southeast flank from Lyman Lake with no ridge crest or pass involved, while itinerary day 2 and the matching timing.sectionBreakdown instead describe gaining a distant East Ridge via Cloudy Pass and Magnolia Mine — a materially different line that matches the neighboring Cloudy Peak Traverse route's own starting point, not this route's own waypoints.
contradictions.internal_resolution: overview + beta + approach + waypoints + approach_variants agree; itinerary.days[1] and timing.sectionBreakdown[1] are the outliers, likely copy-contaminated from the Cloudy Peak Traverse route which does start at Cloudy Pass.

contradictions.internal_resolution: gain_ft/loss_ft and totalNote agree at ~7,500 ft; the itinerary.days gainFt/lossFt values are the outlier and undercount by ~1,850 ft.

contradictions.fact: Order of the summit-ridge scree ramp vs. the final approach to the summit

claims.says: Final 400 ft scree-and-talus ramp ... The final roughly 400 ft to the summit is a scree-and-talus ramp
a scree ramp gains the southwest ridge crest; Class 3 scrambling begins about 400 ft above here
THE CLIMBING STARTS AT A RAMP: from the basin floor, a SCREE-AND-TALUS RAMP of about 400 ft gains the crest of the south-west ridge. Ramp first, ridge second.
Below the gendarmes, descend the scree-and-talus ramp roughly 400 ft into the open basin floor between the two Buttes [i.e. the ramp is the LOWEST section, reached last on descent]

contradictions.why: climbing_route places the 400 ft scree-and-talus ramp as the FINAL step reaching the summit, but waypoints, approach_variants, and descent_text all agree the ramp is the FIRST technical section (basin floor to ridge crest, well below the summit), with the true final approach being ledges on the summit block above ~8,100 ft that climbing_route omits entirely.
contradictions.internal_resolution: waypoints + approach_variants + descent_text (3 fields, with precise directions) agree the ramp comes first; climbing_route's ordering is the outlier and could send a climber looking for an easy scree finish when the actual final terrain is exposed summit-block ledges.

contradictions.fact: Approach/camp line: King Lake + east-ridge notch vs. Buck Creek Pass + Liberty Cap + Louis Creek Basin

claims.says: climb forested, brushy, and open slopes southwestward to King Lake (5,940 ft)... climb directly south to a notch on Buck's east ridge, cross to the south side of the ridge... An alternative, longer approach reaches the peak's west/southwest slopes via Buck Creek Pass and High Pass.
off-trail southwest to King Lake (5,940 ft) ... From King Lake, climb south to a notch on Buck's east ridge and cross to its south side
...contours around Mt. Berge's east side toward King Lake (5,940 ft) and on to an upper basin camp near 6,800 ft
down through King Lake basin, around Mt. Berge, back across Buck Creek...

...into the upper basin below Buck Mountain's south and west aspects (Louis Creek Basin, ~6,700 ft)... pick up the well-used climbers'/boot path that switchbacks up toward Liberty Cap and the High Pass Trail junction (no King Lake mentioned)

descend the pumice and talus slopes back to the Louis Creek Basin camp (~6,700 ft). From there, traverse back east below Liberty Cap to rejoin the boot path down to Buck Creek Pass (no King Lake mentioned)

claims.field: waypoints[2] (Buck Creek Pass, elev 5900, distMi 9.6) / waypoints[3] (Basin below Buck's south/southwest slopes, elev 7400, distMi 11)
claims.says: route passes through Buck Creek Pass, not King Lake
Trinity to Buck Creek Pass, then the High Pass high route around the west side... an easy walk-off down into Louis Creek Basin

contradictions.why: beta's primary paragraph, pitch_detail, both itinerary day notes, and timing.sectionBreakdown all describe reaching camp via King Lake and a notch on Buck's east ridge (with Buck Creek Pass/High Pass explicitly called 'an alternative'); but the top-level approach field, descent_text, the georeferenced waypoints, and approach_variants all instead describe (and only describe) the Buck Creek Pass/Liberty Cap/High Pass/Louis Creek Basin line, never mentioning King Lake at all. The route's fields effectively describe two different, non-overlapping approach lines to two different-elevation, differently-named camps.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Ambiguous — 4 fields favor each line, and the georeferenced waypoints/approach/descent_text/approach_variants track the Buck Creek Pass/Louis Creek Basin line while beta/pitch_detail/itinerary/timing track King Lake; which is truly 'standard' for this route ID cannot be settled from the row alone.
